subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should implicit announce delivery for omitted-delivery `current` and `session:*` jobs be a supported `CronService.add` and declarative contract, and which single helper or boundary should own that policy?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes persisted behavior for direct callers while current code has both normalization-owned and service-owned defaulting paths; selecting the permanent contract and source of truth requires cron owner intent.

options.title: Share one delivery policy
options.body: Keep the direct-service fallback, extract a delivery-specific predicate or resolver, and reuse it from normalization and service creation with sibling-path tests.

options.title: Normalize every creation caller
options.body: Remove service-level defaulting and route gateway, tool, direct, and declarative creation through one normalization boundary before persistence.

options.title: Keep isolated-only fallback
options.body: Reject implicit announce for direct `current` and `session:*` callers and document that those callers must provide delivery explicitly.

recommendation.title: Share one delivery policy
recommendation.body: Keep the direct-service fallback, extract a delivery-specific predicate or resolver, and reuse it from normalization and service creation with sibling-path tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest merged cross-path cron session-target contract was authored and landed through this person's work, providing the strongest evidence of ownership over the intended boundary.
